summary: A bibliography on computer networks and data sharing, arranged into seven subject areas including data structures, description, conversion, management, security, transmission and network design. It also has an author index and updates RFC 243.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 290 is a bibliography of work on computer networks and data sharing. It groups references by topic and includes an author index.

subtitle: A 1972 bibliography of research on computer networks and data sharing.

tldr.problem: Readers needed a way to locate research relevant to computer networks and data sharing across several fields.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC groups references into seven subject areas and provides an index that maps authors to entries.
tldr.outcome: This is a bibliography rather than a protocol, and it updates RFC 243.

today: RFC 290 obsoletes RFC 243. It is a snapshot of literature cited in January 1972.

sections.title: Scope of the Bibliography
sections.content:
Alvin P. Mullery published this bibliography on January 11, 1972, and it updates RFC 243. The bibliography covers work relevant to computer networks and data sharing.

The RFC says that general data structures and data management cover broad subjects, so only especially pertinent entries are included for those areas.
sections.plainLanguage: The document collects research references relevant to sharing data across computer networks. It does not define a protocol.

sections.title: Seven Subject Areas
sections.content:
The bibliography is organized into general data structures, data description, data conversion, data management, data security, data transmission and computer network design.

Entries cite articles, conference papers, workshop papers, technical reports and other works. The author index points readers to the area letter and entry number for each author.
sections.plainLanguage: The seven groups cover how data is organized, described, converted, managed, protected and transmitted, plus network design.

sections.title: Using the Author Index
sections.content:
The author index appears after the seven subject areas. It lists author names with references to the corresponding entries, using a letter for the subject area and a number for the item.

This lets a reader locate an author's listed works without scanning every bibliography section.
sections.plainLanguage: The index connects author names to their entries. Each code identifies a subject area and an item within it.
